used.how: the norm is applied to the y POST_COLLAPSE collapses with the residual's own pre; only attn_norm / ffn_norm read attn_in / ffn_in, so the pass can write the norm instead of y
the normalized y goes into the existing load-time y sites (fork.attn_hc.y / fork.ffn_hc.y) through y_output; no new allocation
norm eps / 1/C as compute common args after the hc scalars and the weight address as a reader common arg (no per-core host cost)
the per-root owner lists are appended after the variable-length per-core args only because they never change on a cache hit; patched values stay in fixed slots / common args
norm_apply / fold / rstd SFPU bodies are template instances with constant DEST indices (no runtime-indexed dst_reg loops)
kept the y tiles in L1 between phases instead of writing and re-reading them from DRAM
did not route the norm through rms_norm's split program (LOCAL mode, one core a row tile); the norm lives in the collapse pass
the statistic is an exact fp32 SFPU sum (the rms_norm fork's is FPU-grade); explains why the result is not bit-identical to off
the y^2 statistic is taken from the packed bf16 y tiles (unpacked exactly), not from an SFPU emulation of the packer's rounding

missing: BRISC word-copy transposes of a 32x32 fp32 tile cost ~8 us (volatile one-word loops); added as DS41-222
a core entering a compute phase cold (no units) keeps compute_kernel_hw_startup's formats; added as DS41-223
tt-probe.sh writes its probes under tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/<name>/probes (outside a perf step's allowed paths: delete them)

overseer.evidence: nothing padded or duplicated: the norm reuses the collapse's y tiles in L1; the scratch keeps its shape; spare cores host the roots only when the grid has them
mhc_post is a C++ device operation (program cache, runtime-arg overrides), not a Python-built program; no Python op added or touched
only the new tests/unit/test_mhc_post_norm.py ran on the 8x4 (6 passed); no fork regression suite
